decisions.rationale: Initial exploration across diverse labels for s1, s3, and s5 to estimate baseline effects against the default configuration.
s1=C strongly lowers f2 while s2=A or s3=A/B strongly reduces f1. Testing s1=C with combinations of s3=A/B and s2=A explores intermediate trade-offs near the current Pareto points.
s4=A strongly reduces f2 while s5=B/C minimizes f1. Testing s1={A,B} with s4=A and s5={B,C} aims to combine low f1 and low f2.

s2=B dramatically reduces f2 to ~2500-3200, while s2=A yields low f1 with high f2. In #2/#3, s5=B/C with s4=B yielded ultra-low f1=2443. We test s5=D with s4=A/B and s2=B variants to improve the low-f2 boundary.
s4=A yields low f2 while s4=B strongly lowers f1. s1=A/B with s2=A and s4=B minimized f1 to ~2443. We test combinations of s1=A/B, s2=A, s3=D/E, and s5=D to discover non-dominated trade-offs.
s4=B drives extreme low f1 when paired with s2=A and s5=D. Meanwhile s4=A with s1=C/D gives lowest f2. Testing s1=E and exploring s3=C variations to push both Pareto frontiers.
s1=E yields the lowest f2 values when s2=B, s4=A, s5=D. Testing s1=E across various s3 choices (C, A, B, E) explores the best trade-offs for minimal f2.
s1=E with s2=B yields the lowest f2, while s4=B and s2=A minimize f1. Evaluating s1=E across alternate s5 and s4 variations to find non-dominated trade-offs.
Exploit the Pareto trade-off around s1=D/C/B with s2=B, s4=A, and s5=D to find optimal compromises between f1 (~5000-6000) and f2 (~2000-2600), testing unvisited s1/s3 combinations.

Investigate combinations along the Pareto boundary: testing s1=E with s3=C or s3=D combined with other low-f2 or low-f1 configurations, and testing s1=E with s2=A on s3=C/E to discover low f2/f1 trade-offs.
Initial exploration across diverse parameter values to assess individual site impacts against the baseline.
s4=A strongly correlates with low f2, while s1=B achieves lowest f1. Combining s1=B, s3=C or D, and s4=A tests if low f1 can be attained with low f2.
s2=B strongly optimizes f2 while s2=A yields low f1. Combining low-f1 features (s1=B, s4=B) with s2=B or testing s3=E with s2=B explores improvements along the Pareto front.
Testing s3=D combined with s2=B and s5=C yields low f2, with s1=D achieving the lowest f2 so far. We explore variations of s5 with s1=D and s3=D to discover trade-offs.
s3=D gives lowest f2, s5=C is optimal across costs, and s1=D has lowest f2 overall. Testing s1=A and alternative s3 options.
s3=D gives low f2 while s5=C is optimal across metrics. Exploring s2=A with s3=D and s1=D/C tests low f1 trade-offs against f2.
Exploit the low f2 region around s3=D, s5=C with s2=B. Testing remaining s5 options (D) with top candidates and varying s1/s4 to map trade-offs in low f1 and low f2 regions.
Test s3=A and s3=B with s2=B, s4=A, s5=C, and s1=D to explore low f2, and check s1=B, s2=A, s3=E, s4=B with other s5 labels to optimize f1.
Evaluating combinations around s3=B with s4=A and s5=C across s1 variants (E, B, C) targeting lower f2 while reducing f1 compared to configuration 37.
Testing s4=B under s3=B with s2=A/B or variants around s3=B, aiming to discover lower f2 or trade-offs since s3=B s4=A s5=C yielded the best f2 (1920).
Initial exploration across major sites s1, s3, and s5 to establish baseline sensitivity relative to the single evaluated baseline.
s4=B appears essential for low f2, while s1=B or A achieved the lowest f1. Testing s1=B with s2=B, s4=B combines low-f1 features with low-f2 features to discover new trade-off points.

s1=B, s3=C, s5=D dominates both f1 and f2 extremes. We test variations around this core to discover intermediate Pareto points and test if s4=A with s2=B or alternative s5 labels reduce f1 while maintaining low f2.
s1=D achieved the best f2 (2112) with s3=C, s4=B, s5=D. Combining s1=D with s3=E or other labels, and testing s5 variations, explores further improvements along the low-f2 edge of the Pareto front.
s1=D and s3=B achieve the lowest f2 (1984). Testing s3=B with other s1 values (C, B) and s4/s2 variants may discover better f1-f2 trade-offs with low f2.
s3=B, s4=B, s5=D yields strong f2. Combining with s2=A explored lowest f1 earlier. Testing s3=B with s2=A across diverse s1 labels (B, C, A) could yield non-dominated points balancing f1 and f2.
Test s4=A combined with s2=B and s3=B/E, and explore s5 variants under the low-f2 baseline s1=D/C to identify optimal trade-offs.
Testing s4=A and s2=A combinations on top of optimal s3 and s5=D settings to explore lower f1 trade-offs and potentially uncover lower f2 high-f1 boundaries.
Testing s3=B with s2=B, s5=D across various s1/s4 settings to optimize the f2-favorable region, and testing s1=E with s2=A / s4=A for f1 minimization.
s3=B minimizes f2 while s5=D is universally optimal. When s3=B, s4 is ignored. Testing s1=D, s2=B with other s5 labels or testing unexplored interactions can refine the Pareto frontier.
Initial exploration across diverse site assignments to assess marginal main effects relative to the baseline.
Evaluations show s4=A significantly reduces f2, while s1=A and s3=A yield low f1. Testing variants combining s1=A, s3=A, and s4=A explores optimal trade-offs between f1 and f2.

s4=B significantly reduces f1, while s2=B with s4=A yields low f2 (~2432). Evaluating s4=B with s5=A and s2=B explores whether lower f1 and intermediate f2 can be achieved. Testing other s5 labels adds diversity.
s1=A with s2=B, s4=A yields low f2 (~2432), while s4=B with s2=A achieved minimal f1 (2443). Testing s1=A, s2=A with varied s5 and s3 values explores potential high-performing f1 compromises.
s1=A with s2=A, s4=B minimizes f1 (especially s5=E, s3=C/A), while s2=B, s4=A minimizes f2. Testing s3=E and combinations targeting low f1 and balanced trade-offs.
Evaluating s3=E with s2=A and s4=B to test for ultra-low f1, and exploring s1=C/D/E with s2=B, s4=A, s5=E to improve f2 and bridge the trade-off.
Test s1=D and other s1 variants with s2=B, s4=B to exploit the low f2 region, and explore s3=E with s4=B combinations to find better trade-offs.
Testing s3={B,C,D} under s1=D,s2=B,s4=A,s5=E to seek even lower f2, and trying s1={B,C,E} with s2=A,s4=B,s5=E to improve f1 tradeoffs.
Combining s1=C and s1=E with s3=E or s3=D and s2=A, s4=B, s5=E may push the lowest f1 even further down while keeping f2 competitive.
Test s1=B with s2=A, s4=B, s5=E to improve f1 at the extreme low-cost end, and test s1=C/D combinations to explore lower f2 and non-dominated trade-offs.
Initial exploration across diverse categorical labels for key unconstrained sites to gauge primary effects on both objectives relative to baseline.
Configurations with s4=B yield significantly lower f2 values, while s1=B showed lowest f1. Testing combinations of s1=B/A with s4=B and varying s3/s5 to map the trade-off frontier.
s2=B drastically reduces f2 while s4=A reduces f1. Config 11 achieved best f2 (2560) with s3=C, s5=B. Testing combinations with s4=A and s2=B or alternative s1/s5 labels explores the sharp trade-off.
Exploration around s3=C, s4=B, s5=B where f2 reaches its minimum (~2112). Testing s1=E and s1=C to see if f2 improves further, and combining s2=A with s4=B on promising templates.
s1=D and s3=E yield the lowest f2 values so far (1984), while s4=A and s2=A strongly reduce f1 at the expense of f2. Testing s1=D/A variants with s3=E and s5 variations.
Combine best low f2 values (s1=D, s2=B, s3=E) with unexplored levels of s5 (C, E) to push the f2 boundary below 1984.
Combining s2=A and s4=A simultaneously produced the lowest f1 (run 3). We test s1 in {B, A} with s2=A, s4=A, and s5=B across promising s3 values (E, B, D) to uncover lower f1 extremes.
Testing s2=A with s4=A and s5=B across s1 variants to push lower f1, and checking whether s3=A yields lowest f1 or improved f2 in promising regions.
Testing s3=E with s4 ignored and variations of s1/s2/s5 to push the lower bounds of f2 and trade off against f1.
Test s1=C with s2=A for low f1, combine s1=D/B with optimal s3/s5 settings to find improvements near the extreme low-f2 and low-f1 boundaries.
